bill.title: Emergency Conservation Program Improvement Act of 2025

industries.rationale: The bill directly expands cost-sharing payments and advance funding for agricultural producers repairing farmland and conservation structures after disasters.
Expanded federal disaster assistance may affect demand for private agricultural and forestry insurance products.

bill.plainSummary: This bill expands two federal programs that help farmers and forest landowners recover from natural disasters. It increases the percentage of costs that can be paid upfront before work begins, extends the time recipients have to use the funds from 60 to 180 days, and makes landowners eligible for assistance when damage from human-caused wildfires spreads due to natural conditions or when federal actions cause the fire. The changes apply to the Emergency Conservation Program and the Emergency Forest Restoration Program.

plain.whoItTouches: Farmers, and anyone who buys food.

bill.title: Whole Milk for Healthy Kids Act of 2025

industries.rationale: The bill directly affects dairy producers and processors by expanding the types of milk schools may purchase and serve.
Schools participating in the lunch program face new training requirements and changes to meal planning and procurement rules.
Food service companies and suppliers to school meal programs would adjust product offerings to meet the expanded milk and nondairy beverage options.

bill.plainSummary: This bill would allow schools participating in the National School Lunch Program to offer whole milk and 2% milk to students, in addition to the low-fat and fat-free options currently required. It would expand nondairy milk alternatives, permit parents (not just doctors) to request milk substitutes for students with dietary restrictions, and exclude milk fat from saturated fat limits in school meals. The bill also requires annual food allergy training and certification for school food service staff.

plain.whoItTouches: Parents of young children. People who use food aid.

That rule gave the CFPB authority to supervise large digital payment apps—specifically, non-bank companies that process at least 50 million transactions per year. bill.title: FIND Act
bill.latestActionText: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs.

industries.rationale: The bill directly protects firearm manufacturers, dealers, and trade associations from discrimination in federal contracting.
Banks and financial institutions that provide services to federal contractors would be affected if they maintain policies restricting business with firearm entities.
Defense contractors frequently hold federal contracts and may need to review policies regarding firearm-related business relationships.
Insurance companies that contract with the federal government would need to ensure their underwriting policies do not discriminate against firearm businesses.

bill.plainSummary: This bill would prohibit federal agencies from awarding contracts to companies that discriminate against firearm manufacturers, dealers, or trade associations. Contractors would be required to certify they have no policies that discriminate against firearm-related businesses and will not adopt such policies during the contract term. The requirement would apply to both prime contractors and subcontractors, with penalties for violations, but would not apply to sole-source contracts.

bill.title: A joint resolution providing for congressional disapproval under chapter 8 of title 5, United States Code, of the rule submitted by the Federal Communications Commission relating to "Addressing the Homework Gap Through the E-Rate Program".

industries.rationale: The bill would eliminate a new revenue stream for wireless carriers and broadband providers who sell hotspots and mobile connectivity services to schools and libraries under the E-Rate program.
The bill would remove schools' and libraries' ability to purchase subsidized internet access equipment for students and patrons, affecting their budgets and service delivery.
The bill would affect manufacturers and vendors of Wi-Fi hotspot devices that would have been purchased through the expanded E-Rate program.

bill.plainSummary: This resolution would overturn a Federal Communications Commission rule that allows schools and libraries to use E-Rate program funds to purchase Wi-Fi hotspots and mobile internet service for students and patrons to use at home. The FCC rule was designed to help students complete homework and access educational resources outside of school buildings. If this resolution passes, that rule would be nullified and schools and libraries would no longer be able to use E-Rate funds for off-campus internet access.

bill.title: Combating Organized Retail Crime Act
bill.latestActionText: Read twice and referred to the Committee on the Judiciary.

industries.rationale: The bill directly addresses organized theft targeting retail operations and e-commerce platforms.
The bill explicitly covers theft from interstate and foreign shipments, affecting logistics and shipping companies.
The bill addresses online marketplaces and social media platforms where stolen goods are sold, potentially creating new compliance obligations.
The bill expands money laundering statutes to cover prepaid cards and gift cards, affecting payment processors and card issuers.

bill.plainSummary: This bill expands federal authority to prosecute organized retail theft and supply-chain crime. It allows prosecutors to aggregate the value of stolen goods over a 12-month period to meet felony thresholds, makes these offenses predicate crimes for money laundering charges, and authorizes asset forfeiture. The bill also creates a temporary coordination center within the Department of Homeland Security to help federal agencies work together on these cases.

bill.title: Fair Access to Banking Act
bill.latestActionText: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Banking, Housing, and Urban Affairs.

industries.rationale: The bill directly regulates how banks and credit unions may deny financial services to customers.
Digital asset firms have frequently reported being denied banking services, making them likely beneficiaries of fair-access requirements.
Firearms businesses have reported service denials from banks citing reputational risk, which this bill would prohibit.
Cannabis and related businesses have faced banking access challenges that this bill's requirements could address.

bill.plainSummary: This bill would restrict banks, credit unions, and payment card networks from refusing service to customers who comply with the law. Financial institutions could only deny service based on documented, quantitative risk standards set in advance, and could not cite reputational concerns as a reason. Violations would trigger penalties including loss of federal deposit insurance, exclusion from electronic payment systems, and potential civil lawsuits by affected customers.

bill.title: Laken Riley Act

industries.rationale: The bill directly imposes new detention mandates on DHS and creates liability exposure for federal agencies, while authorizing state governments to bring suit over immigration enforcement.

The bill creates new grounds for state litigation against the federal government and expands detention requirements, generating demand for legal services in immigration and intergovernmental litigation.

bill.plainSummary: This bill requires the Department of Homeland Security to detain certain non-citizens who are in the country unlawfully and have been arrested for or charged with crimes including burglary, theft, assault on law enforcement, or offenses causing death or serious injury. It also allows state governments to sue the federal government if immigration enforcement decisions or failures—such as releasing detainees, not conducting required asylum interviews, or violating parole limitations—cause harm to the state or its residents, including financial harm exceeding $100.

bill.title: Protecting Access for Hunters and Anglers Act of 2025
bill.latestActionText: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Environment and Public Works.

industries.rationale: The bill directly affects manufacturers and sellers of lead ammunition by limiting federal authority to regulate their products on public lands.
Manufacturers of fishing tackle containing lead would face fewer potential federal restrictions on their products' use.
Sporting goods retailers selling lead ammunition and tackle would benefit from reduced regulatory uncertainty around these product lines.

bill.plainSummary: This bill would prevent three federal agencies—the Fish and Wildlife Service, Bureau of Land Management, and Forest Service—from banning or regulating the use of lead ammunition or fishing tackle on federal lands and waters. The agencies could still impose restrictions in specific locations if they determine, based on field data from that site, that lead use is the primary cause of a wildlife population decline and the state agrees to the regulation. Certain existing regulations would remain in place.

districtAwards.description: P-381 MULTI-MISSION DRY DOCK #1, PORTSMOUTH NAVAL SHIPYARD, KITTERY, ME

DESCRIPTION:THIS AGREEMENT PROVIDES FUNDING UNDER THE INFLATION REDUCTION ACT (IRA) TO NATIVE CDFI NETWORK (NCN).  THE RECIPIENT WILL PROVIDE FUNDING AND TECHNICAL ASSISTANCE TO COMMUNITY LENDERS WHO WILL IN TURN FINANCE CLEAN TECHNOLOGY DEPLOYMENT IN LOW-INCOME AND DISADVANTAGED COMMUNITIES WHILE SIMULTANEOUSLY BUILDING THE CAPACITY OF THE COMMUNITY LENDERS TO DRAW ON THAT CAPITAL TO CATALYZE DEPLOYMENT OF CLEAN ENERGY PROJECTS IN COMMUNITIES ACROSS THE COUNTRYMDASH;ESPECIALLY IN COMMUNITIES THAT HAVE LONG FACED BARRIERS ACCESSING CAPITAL AND THAT MOST NEED THE BENEFITS OF CLEAN TECHNOLOGY PROJECTS. SPECIFICALLY, THE RECIPIENT IS COMMITTED TO DEVELOPING A ROBUST CLEAN ENERGY FINANCE ECOSYSTEM THAT WILL SUPPORT NCN'S COMMUNITY LENDER NETWORK IN DEPLOYING CAPITAL FOR CLEAN ENERGY, ENERGY EFFICIENCY, AND DECARBONIZATION PROJECTS ACROSS NATIVE AND OTHER DISADVANTAGED COMMUNITIES FOR DECADES. NCN WILL WORK WITH 63 COMMUNITY LENDERS WHO HAVE COMMITTED TO SPENDING 100% OF THEIR CAPITALIZATION FUNDING ON CCIA-ELIGIBLE PROJECTS DIRECTLY BENEFITING LOW-INCOME AND DISADVANTAGED COMMUNITIES, INCLUDING THOSE LOCATED ON FEDERALLY RECOGNIZED TRIBAL LANDS.
ACTIVITIES:THE ACTIVITIES THAT NCN ANTICIPATES BEING FUNDED THROUGH THEIR COMMUNITY LENDER NETWORK INCLUDE ROOFTOP AND COMMUNITY SOLAR INSTALLATION, RENEWABLE MICROGRIDS, THE NEW CONSTRUCTION AND RETROFITTING OF NET-ZERO BUILDINGS IN THE PROPOSED COMMUNITIES, INCLUDING RESIDENTIAL BUILDINGS, COMMUNITY HOUSES, MEDICAL CENTERS, AND MUNICIPAL BUILDINGS. ADDITIONAL PROJECTS INCLUDE FINANCING FLEET ELECTRIFICATION, EV CHARGING INFRASTRUCTURE PROJECTS, AND PROVIDING PERSONAL AUTO LOANS FOR EVS OR PLUG-IN HYBRID VEHICLES. 

TECHNICAL ASSISTANCE WILL ADDRESS KNOWLEDGE GAPS AND SUPPORT EXPANSION OF PRODUCTS AND SERVICES TO SUPPORT CLEAN ENERGY FINANCING SUCH AS LOAN PRODUCT DEVELOPMENT AND TRAINING, FINANCE ENGINEERING FOR SUSTAINED FINANCING, CLEAN ENERGY PROJECT DEVELOPMENT AND IMPLEMENTATION, AND OTHER CRITICAL SUPPORT SERVICES. THE PROPOSED PROGRAM WILL ALSO PROVIDE CAPITALIZATION FUNDING TO EACH LENDER TO SUPPORT GREENHOUSE GAS REDUCTION FUND (GGRF) PRIORITY PROJECTS IN NATIVE AND OTHER DISADVANTAGED COMMUNITIES AND SUPPORT THE MEASUREMENT AND VERIFICATION OF PROJECT BENEFITS TO THOSE COMMUNITIES.

districtAwards.recipientName: NEBRASKA DEPARTMENT OF WATER, ENERGY, AND ENVIRONMENT
districtAwards.description:
DESCRIPTION:THE PURPOSE OF THIS AWARD IS TO PROVIDE FUNDING UNDER THE INFLATION REDUCTION ACT (IRA) TO THE NEBRASKA DEPARTMENT OF ENVIRONMENT AND ENERGY. THE RECIPIENT WILL IMPLEMENT GREENHOUSE GAS (GHG) REDUCTION PROGRAMS, POLICIES, PROJECTS, AND MEASURES IDENTIFIED IN A PRIORITY CLIMATE ACTION PLAN (PCAP) DEVELOPED UNDER A CLIMATE POLLUTION REDUCTION GRANTS (CPRG) PLANNING GRANT. ACTIVITIES CONDUCTED THROUGH THIS GRANT WILL BENEFIT ALL RESIDENTS AND VISITORS TO THE STATE OF NEBRASKA THROUGH FOUR MAIN OBJECTIVES: IMPLEMENTATION OF AMBITIOUS MEASURES THAT WILL ACHIEVE SIGNIFICANT CUMULATIVE GHG REDUCTIONS BY 2030 AND BEYOND; PURSUIT OF MEASURES THAT WILL ACHIEVE SUBSTANTIAL COMMUNITY BENEFITS, PARTICULARLY IN LOW-INCOME AND DISADVANTAGED COMMUNITIES; COMPLEMENTING OTHER FUNDING SOURCES TO MAXIMIZE THESE GHG REDUCTIONS AND COMMUNITY BENEFITS; AND, PURSUIT OF INNOVATIVE POLICIES AND PROGRAMS THAT ARE REPLICABLE AND CAN BE 'SCALED UP' ACROSS MULTIPLE JURISDICTIONS. ACTIVITIES:THE ACTIVITIES INCLUDE:
1. PROMOTE ENERGY EFFICIENCY AND ELECTRIFICATION UPGRADES FOR NON-RESIDENTIAL FACILITIES. 
2. INCENTIVES FOR SOLAR PROJECTS ON UNUSED/CONTAMINATED LAND, AG AND INDUSTRIAL FACILITIES, AND PARKING LOT/FEEDLOT SOLAR CANOPIES 
3. RESIDENTIAL PRE-WEATHERIZATION PROGRAM 
4. MEASURES TO REDUCE EMISSIONS IN AGRICULTURAL PRODUCTION 
5. INCENTIVES FOR IRRIGATION WELL ENGINE CONVERSION FROM DIESEL TO ELECTRIC 
6. ESTABLISH HUB-AND-SPOKE ANAEROBIC DIGESTER/BIOGAS HUBS FOR AGRICULTURAL WASTE 
7. INCENTIVES FOR MICRO-SOLAR ARRAYS FOR CRITICAL INFRASTRUCTURE IN LOW-INCOME RURAL COMMUNITIES 
8. INCENTIVES FOR PRODUCTION AND USE OF BIOCHAR TO REDUCE ORGANIC WASTE AND SEQUESTER CARBON IN SOIL 
 

SUBRECIPIENT:ACTIVITIES TO BE IMPLEMENTED EITHER ENTIRELY OR PARTIALLY THROUGH SUBAWARDS INCLUDE:

1.	ENERGY EFFICIENCY AND ELECTRIFICATION UPGRADES FOR NON-RESIDENTIAL FACILITIES
2.	RESIDENTIAL PRE-WEATHERIZATION PROGRAM
3.	MICRO-SOLAR ARRAYS FOR CRITICAL INFRASTRUCTURE IN LOW-INCOME RURAL COMMUNITIES
4.	SOLAR PROJECTS ON UNUSED/CONTAMINATED LAND, FACILITY ROOFTOPS, AND PARKING LOT/FEEDLOT CANOPIES
5.	MEASURES TO REDUCE EMISSIONS IN AGRICULTURAL PRODUCTION
6.	HUB-AND-SPOKE ANAEROBIC DIGESTER/BIOGAS HUBS FOR AGRICULTURAL WASTE
7.	INCENTIVES FOR PRODUCTION AND USE OF BIOCHAR TO REDUCE ORGANIC WASTE AND SEQUESTER CARBON IN SOIL

OUTCOMES:THE ANTICIPATED DELIVERABLES INCLUDE:
1. WORKING WITH EXISTING UTILITY INCENTIVE PROGRAMS TO ENCOURAGE ENERGY EFFICIENCY UPGRADES IN NONRESIDENTIAL BUILDINGS. EXAMPLE INSTALL ELECTRIC HEAT PUMPS TO REPLACE FOSSIL FUEL BOILERS.
2. PROVIDING INCENTIVES TO INSTALLING SOLAR ARRAYS ON NON-GREENFIELD SITES, INCLUDING CONTAMINATED LAND, INDUSTRIAL FACILITIES, AND PARKING LOTS. 
3. PROVIDE FINANCIAL ASSISTANCE WITH HOME IMPROVEMENTS FOR LOW-INCOME RESIDENTS WITH THE INTENT OF MAKING THEM ELIGIBLE FOR THE NEBRASKA WEATHERIZATION ASSISTANCE PROGRAM. 
4. ESTABLISH CARBON INTENSITY (CI) SCORE REGISTRY.
